captured_by: an instrumented COPY of pocket-libre (MIT) run from this Mac over CoreBluetooth via bleak; the reference at ~/Development/pocket-libre was NOT modified

recording.note: The LISTING number (4) and the ANNOUNCED byte count (19770) are different units. Nothing may be sized, bounded, or timed from the listing number.

WHAT_IS_ELIDED_AND_WHY: Every audio notification's BODY. The payload is Nick's real recording. Each audio event keeps its arrival time and its byte LENGTH, which is all a replay needs.
The session key. The authentication frame is recorded as `APP&SK&<REDACTED>` with its true wire length (23 bytes) preserved so a length-sensitive replay is still faithful.

TO REPLAY A BYTE STREAM: slice Tests/FoundryXBrineTests/fixtures/pocket/pocket-fw16-3s.mp3 (already in this repo, provenance-clean, real MPEG-2 L3 32 kbps 16 kHz frames) into the `lengths` array below. The first byte of the real transfer was the MP3 sync word, so the slice needs no preamble prepended — see measurements.preamble_bytes_before_sync_word.

control.note: BIDIRECTIONAL — APP& is written here and MCU& notifies back here

battery.note: read once after connect; forces the bond

A_single_download_audio_subscribed_at_es.purpose: the ground-truth ordering, connect to last byte
A_single_download_audio_subscribed_at_es.audio_subscription_issued: at session establish, BEFORE authentication — i.e. the foundryx ordering, NOT pocket-libre's per-download ordering

events.note: EARLY — foundryx ordering, not the reference's

B_two_downloads_one_session_no_resubscri.purpose: does the audio subscription survive a completed transfer, and is MCU&OFF reproducible
B_two_downloads_one_session_no_resubscri.audio_subscription_issued: once, at session establish; NEVER re-issued between the two downloads; no re-authentication between them either

events.note: EARLY — foundryx ordering, not the reference's

order_of_operations: READ 00002a19 (battery). Forces the bond. Without it 0000ffd2 refuses with CBATTErrorDomain 15 and the device answers nothing anywhere.
subscribe audio 001120a1  [MEASURED: may be done here, before auth]
write APP&U&<date>&<timestamp>  ->  MCU&U&<bytes> on the CONTROL characteristic
audio notifications stream on 001120a1, first one ~1 ms after MCU&U&
MCU&OFF on the CONTROL characteristic, ~0.2-11 ms after the LAST audio chunk
measurements.audio_subscription_evidence: Run A subscribed at establish and got all 19,770 bytes. Run B ran TWO downloads on one subscription with no re-subscribe and no re-auth; both delivered 19,770/19,770 with an identical 82-chunk shape. Subscribing per download (pocket-libre commands.py:245) is therefore NOT a protocol requirement.

announce_latency_ms.note: APP&U write -> MCU&U&<bytes> notification. THIS is the number an 8 s control deadline was supposed to cover; the worst sample is 0.32 s.

chunk_size_bytes.note: 244 = negotiated ATT MTU 247 minus the 3-byte notification header. Short chunks appear mid-stream, not only at the end — do not assume a fixed chunk size.

measurements.preamble_note: The FIRST byte of the FIRST audio notification is 0xFF 0xF3 (frame header 0xFFF348C4, MPEG-2 Layer III, 32 kbps, 16 kHz, mono). There is NO preamble on fw 1.6. PocketBLEProtocolClient.swift's comment above `maximumPreambleBytes` says 'a Pocket prefixes its payload with a short preamble' — measured here, it does not. The trim is harmless (offset 0) but its stated premise is wrong.

terminator.note: SEEN THREE TIMES OUT OF THREE, always immediately after the final audio chunk. Whether it means 'transfer complete' or 'transfer engine off' is not settled by three samples; what IS settled is that it exists, that it lands on the control characteristic, and that a client which stops consuming at the announced byte count will sometimes leave it queued for the NEXT control read.

throughput_bytes_per_second.note: All three are ~21-36 KB/s, which DISAGREES with the ~18 KB/s in foundryx-hearth/reference/pocket-ble-protocol.md. That figure was wall-clock over a whole pocket-libre invocation, which includes its own dead time (below). Design to the SLOW number; measure against these.

measurements.gap_note: Gaps cluster at ~2 ms with a ~26 ms beat every 4 chunks — 4 x 244 B per connection event. The LARGEST gap seen anywhere in three transfers is under 120 ms. An 8,000 ms per-chunk deadline is ~70x the worst observed gap: inter-chunk latency is NOT what an 8 s deadline is failing on.
measurements.reference_implementation_dead_time: pocket-libre's own download loop waits on an audio event BEFORE checking whether the announced byte count is already satisfied (commands.py:265-286). When a transfer completes inside `_send`'s control-wait window — which is what happens for any file small enough — the loop then burns 5 x 5 s of stall timeouts before returning. MEASURED: 26.09 s and 26.15 s of wall clock for a transfer whose audio took 0.54 s. Check the byte count first; do not copy this loop.
